extractedPrimitives.adaptation: Original body, widened the type to retain the embedded message payload.
Original adjacent grouping, replaces CLI registry and schema/classifier lookups with one trusted input validity and read-only predicate.
Original generator and queue type unchanged.
Original transition and terminal vocabulary. Only the used branch subset is surfaced; PGC adds terminal tool_error and output_limit.
Native assistant tool-block accumulation and needsFollowUp decision extracted from the stream handler, applied to one verified full model response.
After-tool nextTurnCount, upper limit, transcript append, and next_turn transition retained. CLI context fields and attachment event are omitted.
Original summary formatter applied after the embedded fork validates exactly one summary block.

preservedBehavior: The query continues on actual tool_use blocks even when the provider stop reason differs. A clean no-tool stop completes even without final text; the host validates the required file or report.
Tool results immediately follow their assistant round. Duplicate, missing and orphaned IDs fail closed, following upstream strict mode. Explicit tool errors remain paired.
Read-only batches merge in completion order, with ten in flight at most. Mutations are exclusive and act as ordering barriers.
Thinking and signatures pass unchanged in the main model trajectory and remain in task memory.

Proactive context pressure uses the CCB effective context window and verified prior API usage as a lower bound. It compacts only complete earlier API rounds. The newest round, immutable input, and all original generated image bytes with their tool/result-part identities remain available.
Compaction runs through the same model callback and counts against the shared model-call and output caps.
adaptations: The provider callback returns one terminal native response. Tool execution during the partial model stream and CLI progress events are omitted.

The embedded task has no interactive commands, stop hooks, CLI attachments/queued notifications, context modifiers, analytics, auth selection, sessions, background agents, or filesystem authority. Tool capabilities and persistence are host-owned.

Provider retries, model fallback, output-limit escalation, reactive replay and speculative token-budget continuation are disabled. A transport error and unknown output retain the requested output reservation. A thrown tool or workspace persistence error stops the query before another model call.
Refusals, missing or unsupported terminal reasons and truncated responses fail closed. In particular, a truncated response cannot execute partial or complete-looking tools.

The default token estimator uses UTF-8 and image approximations, and can be replaced by a host counter. The prior API usage excludes provider fields the host does not expose, such as separate cache-token counters. Compaction leaves the pending main call and at least one output token in the aggregate budget.

The compact fork keeps the upstream no-tools emphasis, chronological detailed summary, concrete file and error references, summary formatter, and recent-round retention. It receives only older working data, no tools or raw reasoning. It requires one summary block and omits CLI transcript paths, all-user-turn reproduction, file rehydration, microcompact, prompt cache compaction, server memory compaction, reactive retries and external summary backends.
Final result exports only final assistant text and bounded usage metadata. Raw thinking, signatures, and transcripts are excluded from the result.

behaviorFixtures.oracle: The checked-in source excerpts execute in every checkout, including clean GitHub CI. Local original source byte verification is an additional check.

oracleBoundary: CI executes the original pinned source fragments in tests/fixtures/embedded-ccb-upstream.json for native tool detection, completion, max turn, transcript update, strict pairing and summary formatting. The fixture pins original file SHA-256 and exact byte/line ranges. The local source checkout, when present, independently verifies the original file and excerpt bytes. Whole upstream QueryEngine, SDK stream, CLI attachments, hooks, reactive retries and original prompt/template stack are outside the tested equivalence.
